blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A processor already sends live traffic to one network. Its terminals run an EMVCo-approved kernel, and it passed a PCI DSS assessment in March. It now signs a contract with another network. On the host side, what stands between it and live traffic on the new link?

options.text: Its host must pass that network's own script, since the link has a specification of its own
options.says: certification proves one host link against one network's specification; another network's certification, the kernel approval and the assessment don't cover it

options.text: Its host must pass a new PCI DSS assessment, since card data will now flow to one more network
options.says: PCI DSS is an audit of how card data is kept, not a message test, and it is not what a network switches live traffic on for

options.text: Nothing more on the host side, since its certification on the first link showed its messages follow ISO 8583
options.says: each network has its own header, private fields and encodings, so one network's certification says nothing about another's

options.text: Nothing more on the host side, since the approved kernel and the March assessment cover the new link as well
options.says: the kernel approval is about the terminal and the assessment about card data; neither tests the host's messages

origin.section: 10.1. Certification Proves One Host Link Against One Network's Specification

questions.stem: A team records the 0100s it sent in its first test-host session. Two hours later, in the second session, it sends the recorded messages again byte for byte. Case 3, an approved purchase on an issued test card, now comes back with 39=94. What happened?

options.text: The host took the request for a repeat, since it carries the STAN and time of one it already answered
options.says: a replayed message repeats fields 11 and 7, and a host that checks for duplicates answers 94; those fields are generated per run

options.text: The host took the request for a repeat, since the same test card was already approved earlier that day
options.says: a duplicate is a message the host has already seen, identified by its STAN and time, not a second purchase on the same card

options.text: The host declined the card itself, since a network's test card approves only once per session
options.says: 94 is duplicate transmission, about the message, not a decline of the card

options.text: The host declined the card itself, since the first approval still holds the amount the case asks for
options.says: 94 says the message was a duplicate; a lack of funds would be a decline such as 51

origin.section: 10.3. A Case Is a Request Template and Every Field Its Answer Must Carry

questions.stem: A tester needs 300 card numbers for a run against the team's own simulator. The generator takes a network's real issuer prefix, adds random digits, and ends each number with a correct check digit, so all 300 pass the acquirer's Luhn check. What has the tester produced?

options.text: Numbers that could be real cardholders' cards, since real cards pass the same check as well
options.says: the check digit only catches typing errors and real cards pass it too, so a generated number may be a real one

options.text: Numbers that could be nobody's cards, since a generated number matches no card an issuer printed
options.says: nothing makes a generated number safe; a test card is one on a list someone issued for testing

options.text: Numbers that count as test cards, since a correct check digit under the prefix is what marks a test card
options.says: the check digit says nothing about who the card belongs to; test cards are issued

options.text: Numbers that count as test cards, since the simulator never forwards them to the real issuer
options.says: where the numbers go doesn't change whose they may be, and a real card number in a log puts every copy under PCI DSS

origin.section: 10.4. A Test Card Is Issued for Testing, and the Luhn Check Only Says It Is Well Formed

questions.stem: During a session the analyst says the terminal ID of STAN 004417 arrived as `2911007` followed by a space, which matches no terminal on the network's side. The team's application log for that message shows `2911007`. What settles who is right?

options.text: The text hex dump of the bytes sent, since the log shows the value before the packager wrote it
options.says: the log shows the message as the program built it; the packager pads a short value on the way out, and only the dump shows the bytes

options.text: The text hex dump of the bytes sent, since the log masks field 41 the way it masks a card number
options.says: the dump is needed because the packager changes the value after the log records it, not because of masking

options.text: The application log line for that STAN, since it records the message the application sent
options.says: the log records the message as built, before padding; the host received the packed bytes

options.text: The application log line for that STAN, since the host's reader pads the field as it unpacks it
options.says: the packager padded the value before it left; only a dump of the bytes shows it

origin.section: 10.5. The Evidence Is the Bytes That Left, Kept as Text and Found by STAN

questions.stem: Three weeks after certification, a team moves to a newer release of its ISO 8583 library. The business logic is untouched, and its own suite passes against its simulator. What should happen before the new build goes live?

options.text: Ask the network whether to certify again, since the network certified the bytes the old release wrote
options.says: the network certified bytes, and a library or packager change can change them

options.text: Ask the network whether to certify again, since the network certified the library release by its number
options.says: the reason to ask is that the bytes may change, not the release number

options.text: Ship it without telling the network, since the network certified what the fields mean, which the library leaves alone
options.says: the network certified the bytes on the link, which the library writes

options.text: Ship it without telling the network, since a passing suite shows the bytes on the link did not change
options.says: the simulator is built from the same reading of the specification; a field written differently on both sides still passes

origin.section: 10.6. The Certified Build Is the One That Goes Live

concepts: A case is a request template whose unique fields are generated per run, graded field by field; a replayed message repeats its STAN and time and meets the host's duplicate check.
Host certification proves one link against one network's specification; an EMV kernel approval, a PCI assessment or another network's certification does not cover it.
The network certified bytes, so a change of library, packager definition or channel after certification is cleared with the network before it goes live.
The log shows the message as the program built it and the packager may change it on the way out, so the evidence is a text hex dump of the bytes, found by STAN.
A number with a correct check digit under a network's prefix may belong to a cardholder, since every printed card passes the check.
